priorVersion.title: Determining what the agreement requires
priorVersion.summary: Interpretation determines the meaning and scope of the parties’ agreement. It asks what their words and conduct mean in the relevant setting, including the evidence the governing law permits the court to consider.
priorVersion.notes:
Begin with the language and the issue in dispute. A disagreement about meaning is different from a claim that an additional agreement should be included. The parol evidence rule addresses the effect of a final written agreement on earlier or contemporaneous terms. Rules about extrinsic evidence address what may be considered in interpreting the words that remain.

Pacific Gas and Trident examine a context-sensitive approach and its consequences. W.W.W. Associates and Greenfield emphasize the written language where it is unambiguous under their approach. Frigaliment and Hurst show the importance of commercial meaning. Nanakuli, Figgie, and Columbia Nitrogen address established practices that may explain or supplement an agreement. These decisions cannot be reduced to a universal instruction either to ignore context or to admit all context.

The case index includes relevant decisions from formation and performance because interpreting a commitment also determines whether a promise exists, how discretion is constrained, and whether conduct amounts to breach.
